info.title: Nudge-A-Tron 5000 API
info.description:
Nagging reminders: a reminder fires on a schedule and keeps nagging, more insistently each time, until it's acknowledged.

Within v0 the API only grows: clients must ignore response fields and enum values they don't know. Errors are RFC 9457 problem details (`application/problem+json`).

Strength.description: How insistently a reminder nags (see ADR 0005).

Cap.description: When an unanswered occurrence gives up. Unset fields use the system default (24 h, 20 attempts).

dtstart.description: Local wall-clock time in `timezone`. It must exist there (not in a DST gap).

timezone.description: An IANA time zone name, exactly as listed (not an offset such as +05:00).

rrule.description: RFC 5545 RRULE without the `RRULE:` prefix. FREQ may not be SECONDLY; BYSECOND takes one value; COUNT and INTERVAL are 1–1000; at most 500 characters. Occurrences are always at least a minute apart.

nextCursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; null on the last page.

EventNAG_SENT.description: A nag was queued for delivery.

EventSEND_FAILED.description: Delivering a nag failed. `nextTryAt` is null once delivery gives up.

EventDEFERRED_QUIET.description: A nag was deferred to the end of quiet hours.

EventSUPERSEDED.description: The next occurrence replaced this unanswered one.

QuietHours.description: A daily window in the user's time zone, [start, end). start > end crosses midnight.

patch.description: A schedule change (dtstart, timezone or rrule) moves the next occurrence to the new schedule. An open occurrence keeps nagging; strength and cap apply from its next nag.

delete.description: Stops the reminder: it gets no more occurrences, and its open occurrence is cancelled. Its occurrences and their events stay readable by id.
